questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: An English-speaking country, cultural diversity, high academic standards, nature experiences

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: In general, I think it was easy to find the information needed. Remember to use your McGill Email since most information regarding course registration, health insurance, orientation, etc. is emailed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I participated in an orientation day for international students (social event) and the Faculty of Law hosted an Information session for exchange students about course registration, course credits, deadlines, grades etc. In general, the Student Affairs Office (SAO) at the Faculty of Law was very helpful and responded quickly to my emails.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy. I just used Google, however, I know many of my friends used different Facebook Groups or Airbnb.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived downtown close to Old Montreal and Old Port and within walking distance of McGill, which I enjoyed. Even though the metro works well, I recommend living within walking (or biking) distance of McGill. Most people who lived in Plateau or Mile End enjoyed it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
I think the registration process was unnecessarily complicated. You need to use Minerva. I found a guide and a video that described the registration process.
https://www.mcgill.ca/students/courses/add/register

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The SAO. They reply quickly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Rather successful. But only because of the add/drop period.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: First of all, registration opens later for exchange students meaning that many courses were already full when I registered. Moreover, it is first come first served so remember the registration date! Second, there is a course change period (add/drop period) in the first two weeks where it is possible to add/drop courses. I changed two of my courses in this period. I would suggest using "seat alert - McGill" where you receive notifications on your McGill Email if there is an available spot in a course. That way, you do not have to look in Minerva all the time. Third, it is relatively easy to get the professor's approval if you want to enroll in a graduate course. Fourthly, remember to register for a waitlist as early as possible (but you are only permitted to register for one waitlist per term).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It was a bit too theoretical and philosophical to my liking. At first glance, the readings seem overwhelming. However, my impression was that no one reads it all, and it is possible to find different summaries of the articles on the following website:
https://www.pubdocs.lsa-aed.ca

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Due to the agreement between McGill and UCPH I was considered an undergraduate student even though I am a graduate student at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style differed significantly from the UCPH. There are no lectures, and the style of teaching is more discussion and presentation based. Generally, students are expected to participate actively. Furthermore, the method of evaluation differs from course to course (midterms, participation, final exam, etc.), and there is no reading break.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Private International Air Law
European Union Law(1) 
Canadian Legal History 
Immigration and Refugee Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Private International Air Law. It focuses on different sources of private air law, unification of law of liability, conflicts of law, etc. The most practical course. It is a graduate course, so you need the professor's approval.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: My room was furnished, however, I had to buy everything else (pillow, pillowcase, duvet, towels, cutlery, plates, etc.) But there is an IKEA only 30 minutes from Montreal (close to the airport). Or you can try Dollarama.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were more expensive than I expected. Coffee was cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would sign up for Frosh, which is part of the orientation week. It is a series of events organized by university groups, clubs, or Faculty-student associations. Those of signed up for McGill Outdoors Frosh were very satisfied.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of things going on at McGill. I bought a membership to the McGill gym, you can sign up for different competitions (e.g., Badminton), Open Air Pub (OAP) which is a student-run music festival, barbecue, and bar in the first two weeks,

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Follow LSA on Instagram. They host many social activities: Coffeehouse each Thursday, Ski Trip, Movie Night, Yoga, Karaoke, Moka Monday, etc. A great way to meet other students and socialize.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hiking, explore the different areas in Montreal (entirely different), eat bagels (St-Viateur Bagel or Fairmount Bagel), see an Ice hockey Game, and visit Toronto, Ottawa, Mont Tremblant, Boston, New York, or Quebec City.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. However, Montreal is located in the French-speaking part of Canada so you may encounter a language barrier. For instance, most official information (e.g., in the metro) is only in French, and some people only speak French. I do not speak French and still found it easy to adjust.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: People at McGill are young but also very open-minded, talkative, and friendly. Speak to the other students in your different courses.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language (French).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People's friendliness, talkativeness, politeness, etc.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Participate in the different social activities in the beginning (use WhatsApp to connect with people) 
Do not stress about not getting the courses you want in the first round - there is a lot of mobility in the add/drop period. 
Enjoy your time!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Meeting (and becoming friends) with people from around the world (and from Denmark). 
Exploring a new country/culture and knowing more about the locals' culture and way of life. 
Learning more about myself.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Living far away from family and friends.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: A once-in-a-lifetime experience! I recommend studying abroad to everyone.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
